citation: Karl, D., 'Forecasting e-commerce consumer returns: a systematic literature review', Management Review Quarterly 75(3), 1-56
research_question_or_objective: Synthesizes literature on return forecasting, identifying predictors, algorithms, and methodological gaps in retail returns
dataset_and_sample_size: 25 peer-reviewed papers (searches through mid-2022) across IS, OM, and marketing
ground_truth_definition: Binary return indicator (returned vs retained) from retailer order logs
methodology_and_algorithms: Systematic review and taxonomical mapping across predictive algorithms (ML, Logit, Random Forest, Deep Learning)
baselines_used: Historical baseline return rates and basic logit models
metrics_reported: Classification accuracy, AUC-ROC, F1-score, return rate reduction
key_findings: Return forecasting is dominated by quantitative retailer case studies; consumer demographics and basket composition are primary predictors
explicit_limitations: Search cutoff mid-2022; excludes reverse logistics anomaly detection and physical inspection; focused on pre-return probability rather than physical condition verification
future_work_recommendations: Calls for research linking return forecasts to reverse operational execution, return timing, and warehouse disposition costs
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Proves predicting WHETHER a customer returns an item is established prior art; TriNetra must focus on physical condition/identity verification across handovers

citation: Elia, G., Ghiani, G., Manni, E., & Margherita, A., 'A system for anomaly detection in reverse logistics: an application into an e-commerce company', Measuring Business Excellence 28(2), 222-242
research_question_or_objective: Develops an operational framework and dashboard for continuous anomaly detection in e-commerce reverse logistics
dataset_and_sample_size: Single e-commerce fashion retailer; internal return records + stakeholder interviews
ground_truth_definition: Historical return anomaly categories logged by warehouse operators
methodology_and_algorithms: Algorithmic anomaly detection, process KPI monitoring, and operational exception dashboard
baselines_used: Standard manual triage and historical reactive inspection
metrics_reported: Time to detect anomalies, data accuracy %, completeness of analysis %, cost efficiency %
key_findings: Continuous reverse logistics monitoring shifts management from reactive crisis resolution to proactive exception handling; classifies anomalies by category and root cause
explicit_limitations: Single-company case study in fashion; lacks statistical multi-baseline benchmark; does not evaluate doorstep OBD or carrier handover chains
future_work_recommendations: Authors explicitly call for validation in other industrial sectors, geographies, and varied logistics architectures
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Confirms generic returned-goods anomaly detection is established; TriNetra's novelty cannot be 'anomaly detection in returns' but must address cross-stage handover continuity and Indian OBD boundaries

citation: Johna, S., Shah, B. J., & Kartha, P., 'Refund fraud analytics for an online retail purchases', Journal of Business Analytics 3(1), 56-66
research_question_or_objective: Predicts agent-level refund fraud in e-commerce customer support queues to optimize manual audit allocation
dataset_and_sample_size: Proprietary transactional dataset from an online retail business; rare-event sample
ground_truth_definition: Internal loss-prevention audit finding of confirmed fraudulent refund transactions by agents
methodology_and_algorithms: Penalized Likelihood Logistic Regression (Firth's Logit) for rare-event binary classification
metrics_reported: Capture rate in top 5% audit queue, Lift, Sensitivity, Specificity
key_findings: Penalized logit significantly improves fraud capture in the top 5% audited transactions without overwhelming human auditors
explicit_limitations: Targets internal agent refund collusion, not consumer physical substitution or courier tampering; proprietary data not publicly accessible
future_work_recommendations: Recommends expanding predictive features to multi-channel customer communications and automated dispute triage
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Proves ML-driven refund fraud ranking is prior art; TriNetra's problem is distinct: multi-actor physical evidence verification rather than internal customer-service agent audit ranking

citation: Mishra, A., & Dutta, P., 'Sustainable reverse logistics in e-commerce: a comprehensive literature review with challenges and research opportunities', Annals of Operations Research 358(1), 275-329
research_question_or_objective: Comprehensive synthesis of 240 papers on e-commerce reverse logistics, return policies, handling costs, and sustainability
dataset_and_sample_size: 240 peer-reviewed articles analyzed across OM, sustainability, and logistics journals
ground_truth_definition: N/A (Methodological and conceptual review across literature)
methodology_and_algorithms: Systematic literature review, bibliometric mapping, and thematic content analysis
metrics_reported: Publication growth trends, thematic cluster frequencies, methodological distributions
key_findings: Reverse logistics research is rapidly expanding but heavily skewed toward forward-reverse network design and environmental disposition; operational verification at handovers remains under-researched
explicit_limitations: Broad thematic scope limits granular algorithmic comparison of sensor-based inspection; focuses on macro sustainability
future_work_recommendations: Calls for empirical investigations into digital tracking technologies, return handling friction, and consumer-retailer dispute dynamics
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Confirms macro reverse logistics is saturated; anchors TriNetra's specific contribution in micro-level handover evidence continuity and dispute resolution friction

citation: Shang, G., Ghosh, B. P., & Galbreth, M. R., 'Optimal Retail Return Policies with Wardrobing', Production and Operations Management 26(7), 1315-1332
research_question_or_objective: Determines optimal return windows, restocking fees, and pricing when consumers exhibit opportunistic wardrobing behavior
dataset_and_sample_size: Stylized analytical game-theoretic model of consumer purchasing, usage, and return decisions
ground_truth_definition: Mathematical definition of wardrobing: purchase with intent to consume temporarily and return for full refund
methodology_and_algorithms: Stochastic optimization, utility-maximizing game theory, and equilibrium analysis
baselines_used: Standard full-refund lenient return policy benchmark
metrics_reported: Retailer profit, return volume, wardrobing rate, social welfare
key_findings: Lenient return policies maximize customer acquisition but create a deadweight loss from wardrobing; optimal policy balances restocking fees with product margins
explicit_limitations: Purely mathematical model; assumes perfect knowledge of customer utility distributions; does not model physical verification or item swapping
future_work_recommendations: Recommends empirical testing of return fee elasticity and technological solutions to detect pre-worn garments
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Establishes that theoretical modeling of return opportunism is mature; TriNetra must deliver operational evidence-adjudication rather than abstract game theory

citation: King, T., & Dennis, C., 'Unethical consumers: deshopping behaviour using the qualitative analysis of theory of planned behaviour', Qualitative Market Research 9(3), 282-296
research_question_or_objective: Investigates consumer motivations, rationalizations, and retailer management dilemmas regarding fraudulent deshopping / return abuse
dataset_and_sample_size: Focus groups with consumers and in-depth interviews with retail store and loss-prevention managers
ground_truth_definition: Self-reported consumer admission of purchasing goods with premeditated intent to return after use
methodology_and_algorithms: Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) qualitative coding and retail loss-prevention policy analysis
baselines_used: Qualitative comparative case analysis across retail store formats
metrics_reported: Thematic recurrence rates, consumer rationalization categories, staff confrontation anxiety
key_findings: Consumers neutralize guilt by perceiving retailers as faceless corporate entities able to absorb losses; retail staff feel unempowered to confront suspicious returns without objective proof
explicit_limitations: Qualitative self-report in brick-and-mortar retail; precedes modern e-commerce doorstep delivery and camera/scale telematics
future_work_recommendations: Urges development of objective point-of-return verification technologies to remove emotional burden from frontline staff
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Provides foundational behavioral taxonomy for return abuse; directly motivates TriNetra's objective evidence collection to eliminate subjective human accusation

citation: Bhattacharya, M., 'A Dynamic Mechanism for Mitigating Fraudulent Returns in e-Commerce', SSRN Working Paper 6803038
research_question_or_objective: Proposes dynamic risk scoring, return bonds, and audit mechanisms to curb consumer return fraud while protecting honest buyers
dataset_and_sample_size: Three-player mathematical formulation: Customer, Platform, and Third-Party Seller
ground_truth_definition: Theoretical definition of fraudulent return: returning non-authentic or damaged goods while claiming full refund
methodology_and_algorithms: Dynamic multi-period game theory, reputation scoring with score aging, and incentive-compatible contract design
baselines_used: Static return policy without risk scoring
metrics_reported: Equilibrium fraud rate, platform transaction volume, seller retention, consumer surplus
key_findings: A dynamic mechanism combining risk-adjusted return bonds and audit probability mitigates fraud while maintaining market liquidity; recognizes return legitimacy is imperfectly observable
explicit_limitations: Theoretical working paper without real-world physical deployment data; relies on stylized audit accuracy assumptions
future_work_recommendations: Calls for empirical validation of dynamic scoring algorithms in live e-commerce marketplaces
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Demonstrates that imperfect observability of returns is already recognized theoretically; TriNetra's gap is delivering the actual physical evidence architecture that makes audits reliable

citation: Kar, B., Das, P. P., & Mohapatra, S., 'Exploring Product Return Behavior in E-Commerce: Insights from an Emerging Market Context', Indian Journal of Marketing 54(5), 26-44
research_question_or_objective: Identifies behavioral and situational determinants driving high e-commerce product return rates in the Indian emerging market
dataset_and_sample_size: Survey of online shoppers across urban India (structured questionnaire)
ground_truth_definition: Self-reported return frequency and stated reasons for returning online purchases
methodology_and_algorithms: Factor analysis, multi-variable regression, and structural equation modeling on consumer survey responses
metrics_reported: Variance explained (R-squared), regression coefficients, factor loadings
key_findings: Return behavior in India is heavily driven by impulsive buying, delivery encounter friction, product dissonance, and opportunistic experimentation enabled by cash-on-delivery
explicit_limitations: Self-reported consumer survey; prone to social desirability bias; does not inspect physical logistics records or audited fraud cases
future_work_recommendations: Recommends examining operational interventions during delivery and return pickup to minimize post-purchase dissonance
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Provides empirical proof of India's unique return friction and cash-on-delivery opportunism; confirms survey data cannot serve as physical ground truth for TriNetra

citation: Saxena, S., Chawla, V., & Richa, 'Should e-returns services be one-size-fits-all for consumers? Segmentation using return policy promises and constraints', International Journal of Physical Distribution & Logistics Management 55(5), 452-481
research_question_or_objective: Investigates consumer heterogeneity in valuing e-commerce return policies and derives customer segments to optimize return services
dataset_and_sample_size: Study 1: 23 in-depth interviews; Study 2: 257 consumer ranking survey respondents in India
ground_truth_definition: Consumer-perceived value and preference rankings across return policy dimensions
methodology_and_algorithms: Mixed-methods: qualitative thematic analysis followed by rank-order logit modeling
metrics_reported: Log-likelihood, McFadden's pseudo-R-squared, segment preference coefficients
key_findings: Consumers are fundamentally non-homogeneous: identifies three distinct segments: Inconvenience Haters, Rapid Reliable Response Cravers, and Refund Worriers
explicit_limitations: Measures consumer perceptions and policy preferences, not physical product fraud or parcel tampering; full text requires subscription access
future_work_recommendations: Calls for empirical evaluation of differentiated reverse logistics workflows and technology-enabled return tracking
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Directly informs TriNetra's economic model: return friction must avoid treating all consumers as fraudsters; automated evidence checks must support rapid refunds for low-risk segments

citation: Bhavya, N. et al., 'Predictive Modeling of Customer Satisfaction in Computer Hardware Product Returns: A Case Study in Bengaluru, India', Journal of Information Systems Engineering and Management 10(12s), 1870
research_question_or_objective: Predicts customer satisfaction during computer hardware returns and identifies key operational bottleneck factors
dataset_and_sample_size: 223 customer survey responses from e-commerce computer hardware buyers in Bengaluru
ground_truth_definition: Customer-rated satisfaction score (Likert scale) regarding return process
methodology_and_algorithms: Supervised classification: Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM)
metrics_reported: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score across classifiers
key_findings: Processing time, pickup ease, and transparent refund status are the strongest predictors of customer satisfaction in hardware returns
explicit_limitations: Small regional sample (n=223); survey-derived target variable; does not verify hardware physical condition or serial/IMEI provenance
future_work_recommendations: Suggests integrating real-time telemetry and IoT tracking into return management to enhance transparency
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Demonstrates that standard ML classification is already applied to Indian return survey data; TriNetra must differentiate by processing objective physical sensor packets rather than survey satisfaction

citation: Flipkart Internet Pvt. Ltd., 'Open Box Delivery Terms & Conditions'
research_question_or_objective: Defines the contractual and operational protocol for Open Box Delivery (OBD) of high-value electronics and appliances
dataset_and_sample_size: National operating terms published on platform website
ground_truth_definition: Customer acceptance (OTP provision) vs rejection at doorstep
methodology_and_algorithms: Mandatory doorstep unboxing by delivery associate; physical verification of outer condition, model, and missing components prior to OTP sharing
baselines_used: Standard doorstep delivery with sealed parcel handover
metrics_reported: Binary delivery outcome: Accepted (Delivered) vs Rejected (Return to Origin)
key_findings: Restricts subsequent claims for physical damage, wrong item, or missing accessories once OTP is validated; excludes functional testing from doorstep scope
explicit_limitations: Policy document only; does not disclose compliance rates, delivery executive rushing behavior, or subsequent dispute adjudication data
future_work_recommendations: Platform updates policy iteratively; no academic research disclosure on doorstep verification error rates
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Defines the exact operational policy boundary in India: OBD covers external visual appearance and components but explicitly excludes functional testing and latent defect verification

citation: Department of Consumer Affairs / Press Information Bureau, 'Government amends E-Commerce Rules to strengthen consumer protection and promote transparency'
research_question_or_objective: Discloses annual consumer grievance statistics from National Consumer Helpline and announces 2026 E-Commerce Amendment Rules
dataset_and_sample_size: 1771622 total grievances registered on NCH in 2025; 511196 e-commerce grievances (approx 29%)
ground_truth_definition: Formal consumer complaints registered through NCH portal and UMANG app
methodology_and_algorithms: National grievance census, categorization by sector, and statutory rulemaking
baselines_used: Historical annual grievance distributions from prior years
metrics_reported: Total grievance volume, percentage share by industry sector
key_findings: E-commerce is the single largest contributor to consumer grievances in India (29%); amendments mandate transparent complaint copies, grievance tracking, and seller disclosures
explicit_limitations: Aggregate grievance counts represent consumer allegations, not adjudicated fraud or audited operational error rates; no parcel-level data
future_work_recommendations: Government mandates implementation of enhanced dispute resolution tracking by 1 January 2027
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Provides authoritative macro context on the dispute crisis in India; proves consumer dissatisfaction is immense but confirms grievance counts cannot be used as training labels for fraud

citation: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission Central Mumbai, 'Mr. Rushabh Maroo v. CrossBeats', CC/132/2022
research_question_or_objective: Adjudicates consumer complaint where seller rejected return/refund of defective earbuds due to lack of customer unboxing video
dataset_and_sample_size: Adjudicated judicial dispute proceeding (Order dated 09 February 2024)
ground_truth_definition: Judicial finding of Deficiency in Service and Unfair Trade Practice under Consumer Protection Act 2019
methodology_and_algorithms: Judicial evidentiary review under Section 35 of Consumer Protection Act 2019
baselines_used: Opposite party terms & conditions requiring uninterrupted unboxing video
metrics_reported: Refund of purchase price (Rs 1899) with 9% interest + Rs 5000 compensation + Rs 3000 costs
key_findings: A seller cannot unilaterally impose an 'unboxing video' requirement post-purchase to deny statutory return rights; one-sided evidentiary demands are unfair trade practices
explicit_limitations: Single legal adjudication; proceeding was ex-parte against seller; does not establish operational fraud rates across the industry
future_work_recommendations: Demonstrates that platforms must possess independent, contemporaneous handover evidence rather than shifting proof entirely to consumers
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Establishes critical legal precedent: Indian consumer courts reject corporate policies demanding customer unboxing videos, proving retailers need auditable delivery-agent evidence chains

citation: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission Adilabad, 'Consumer v. Flipkart Internet Pvt. Ltd.', CC/24/2025
research_question_or_objective: Adjudicates dispute where consumer identified wrong model (Qubo Q600 vs Q500) during OBD and delivery associate allegedly refused to record failed delivery
ground_truth_definition: Judicial finding of deficiency in service and failure of doorstep verification escalation
methodology_and_algorithms: Judicial review of consumer complaint, delivery notes, and customer support communications
baselines_used: Ex-parte defense by e-commerce platform and seller
metrics_reported: Full refund + compensation for mental harassment + punitive damages
key_findings: Demonstrates a failure mode where frontline delivery associate fails to follow OBD protocol, forcing consumer into prolonged customer-care escalation despite spotting wrong item
explicit_limitations: Single case study; legal news reporting; companies proceeded ex-parte; cannot generalize failure frequency nationwide
future_work_recommendations: Highlights need for tamper-proof mobile capture apps that allow immediate doorstep failed-verification logging
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Provides documented evidence of a specific OBD workflow breakdown: delivery agent refusal/inability to register doorstep discrepancy, directly justifying TriNetra's edge logging

citation: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission Kurnool, 'Consumer v. Perfume 24x7', CC/71/2025
research_question_or_objective: Adjudicates wrong-product delivery dispute where consumer documented received counterfeit/different perfume using photos and video
ground_truth_definition: Judicial finding of deficiency in service and punitive damages for supplying substitute product
methodology_and_algorithms: Judicial evaluation of contemporaneous photographic evidence and unboxing records
baselines_used: Merchant denial and refusal of reverse pickup
metrics_reported: Punitive damages of Rs 200000 + refund of purchase amount + litigation costs
key_findings: Contemporaneous visual documentation provided by consumer was decisive in proving product substitution and securing substantial punitive relief against seller
explicit_limitations: Single case; illustrates extreme scenario of punitive damages; not representative of routine return disputes
future_work_recommendations: Emphasizes necessity of verifiable item identification (barcodes, serials) at fulfillment and delivery to prevent substitution
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Proves Indian courts heavily weigh contemporaneous evidence in wrong-item disputes, showing that auditable handover documentation protects both honest consumers and compliant sellers

citation: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission Rangareddy, 'Consumer v. E-Commerce Platform', CC/104/2025
research_question_or_objective: Adjudicates reverse logistics dispute where platform denied refund after pickup, alleging sunglasses were returned scratched with missing accessories
ground_truth_definition: Judicial finding of deficiency in service due to absence of continuous evidence linking return condition to consumer
methodology_and_algorithms: Judicial review of reverse pickup receipt, customer communication, and warehouse rejection claim
baselines_used: Platform claim of post-receipt return inspection failure
metrics_reported: Refund of Rs 17839 + Rs 5000 compensation for deficiency + Rs 5000 litigation costs
key_findings: Platform failed to prove the item was damaged by the consumer because the delivery agent accepted the item without documenting scratches at pickup; evidence chain was broken
explicit_limitations: Single case; secondary news report from Financial Express; full primary order text not independently retrieved; exact docket number CC/104/2025 is inferred, not confirmed
future_work_recommendations: Demonstrates critical operational gap: failure of reverse pickup agents to document condition at doorstep shifts liability to platform
tri_netra_relevance_and_distinction: Directly validates TriNetra's core thesis: without continuous evidence linking return pickup condition to warehouse receiving, platforms cannot legally or responsibly attribute damage
